overview: White develops the knight to the rim, intending Nf4 or g3/Bxh3-proof set-ups, and keeps the centre flexible. Black normally takes the centre with ...d5 or ...e5 and White follows with f4, g3, Nf4 and c4, or plays for a Reti/English-like set-up. The position is playable but slightly inferior, so the game becomes a slow manoeuvring one where Black has the easier time.

white_ideas.idea: Reroute the knight to f4 or f2 and play g3, Bg2 and c4 for a Reti-style fianchetto set-up.
Play f4 and Nf2 (Krazy Kat) to build a Dutch-like centre with e4 later.

black_ideas.idea: Occupy the centre at once with ...d5 and ...e5 and develop normally.
Play ...Bxh3 to wreck White's kingside pawns, the standard answer after an early g3 and Bg2.

typical_structures.structure: Reti-style set-up: pawns on c4, d3 or d4, g3 with a bishop on g2.
Dutch-like f4 set-up against Black's e5/d5 centre.

character.notes: Quiet flank development with no forcing lines; neither side is forced into risk early.

gambit.notes: No material is offered; the Ammonia line 1...Nh6 is a mirror, not a gambit.

soundness.notes: Playable but slightly worse than central moves because the knight is misplaced on h3; not refuted.

structure.notes: Flank opening: the centre is undecided after 1.Nh3, so Flexible.

approach.notes: Strong players seldom choose 1.Nh3; it is a surprise move.

level.notes: Little theory and clear ideas, but inferior to 1.Nf3, so not a first-repertoire choice.

sublines_that_differ.name: Krazy Kat
sublines_that_differ.how: A rare attempt at a Dutch-style centre that gives Black an easy lead.

sublines_that_differ.name: Ammonia Opening
sublines_that_differ.how: Black copies the knight move; a joke-level mirror line.

character.reason: Quiet flank opening with no forcing play and few ways to lose quickly.

structure.reason: Flank opening with the centre still undecided.

level.reason: Simple ideas but not a sound repertoire starting point.

plans.reason: White usually builds a g3 and Bg2 set-up.
